Methacholine Challenge Test or Bronchoprovocation Test or Bronchial Challenge Test
sampleRequirement: The Methacholine Challenge Test, also known as the Bronchoprovocation Test or Bronchial Challenge Test, is a specialized diagnostic procedure used to assess airway hyperresponsiveness. During this test, patients inhale increasing concentrations of methacholine, a substance that causes the airways to narrow. By measuring lung function before and after inhalation, the test determines the sensitivity of the airways and helps diagnose conditions such as asthma. The Methacholine Challenge Test is a safe and effective way to evaluate the presence and severity of airway hyperresponsiveness, providing crucial information for accurate diagnosis and guiding appropriate treatment strategies for patients with suspected asthma.

Pulmonary Function Testing (Pre and Post-bronchodilator test)
sampleRequirement: Pulmonary or Respiratory Function Testing, including pre and post-bronchodilator tests, is a vital diagnostic tool used to evaluate lung function. In this procedure, patients undergo a series of breathing maneuvers to measure lung volume, capacity, and airflow rates. The pre-bronchodilator test establishes a baseline assessment, while the post-bronchodilator test assesses the response to a bronchodilator medication, often used in the treatment of respiratory conditions such as asthma or COPD. This comprehensive evaluation provides valuable information about airway obstruction and the effectiveness of bronchodilator therapy, aiding physicians in diagnosing and managing respiratory disorders for optimal patient care.
